name: Pulmonary Veno-Occlusive Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical, radiological, and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Histological evidence of widespread occlusion of small pulmonary veins by fibrous tissue
Presence of pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization
Characteristic high-resolution CT findings including centrilobular ground-glass opacities, septal lines, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as left heart disease or chronic thromboembolic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of venous occlusion plus clinical and imaging evidence of pulmonary hypertension with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is definitive but often high risk; diagnosis may be presumptive based on clinical and imaging features.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
searchTerms: oxygen deficiency not improved by oxygen

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pulmonary arterial hypertension confirmed by right heart catheterization
searchTerms: confirmed high pressure in lung arteries by catheter
pulmonary arterial hypertension diagnosed via heart catheter
lung artery hypertension verified by catheter test
fatigue due to poor oxygen levels
sudden loss of consciousness at rest

rare.notes: Occurs due to increased capillary pressure
searchTerms: pulmonary edema following blood vessel dilator use

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) indicating right heart strain
imaging: High-resolution CT showing centrilobular ground-glass opacities
other: Right heart catheterization demonstrating elevated pulmonary arterial pressures with normal pulmonary capillary wedge pressure

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of venous occlusion on histology
Lack of characteristic CT findings such as septal lines
Presence of chronic thromboembolic material on imaging

redFlags: Pulmonary edema triggered by vasodilator therapy
Severe pulmonary hypertension with right heart failure signs
references: Montani D, et al. Pulmonary veno-occlusive disease. Eur Respir J. 2009;33(1):189-200.
Eyries M, et al. EIF2AK4 mutations cause pulmonary veno-occlusive disease, a recessive form of pulmonary hypertension. Nat Genet. 2014;46(1):65-69.
Simonneau G, et al. Updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2013;62(25 Suppl):D34-41.
